name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

122	/-! ## §1. Abelian-group structure on the relative Picard quotient
123	
124	The Picard group `Pic(X)` of any scheme is canonically an abelian group
125	under tensor product of line bundles (Stacks tag 01CR; the inverse of
126	`[L]` is `[L⁻¹] = [Hom_{O_X}(L, O_X)]`). The pullback map
127	`π_T^* : Pic(T) → Pic(C ×_k T)` of
128	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection`
129	respects this structure: it sends `O_T ↦ O_{C ×_k T}` (the structure
130	sheaf is preserved by inverse image) and is multiplicative on tensor
131	products (Stacks 01HH for invertibility, Mathlib's
132	`Scheme.Modules.pullback` for the underlying multiplicativity).
133	
134	Therefore `π_T^* Pic(T)` is a subgroup of `Pic(C ×_k T)`, and the
135	quotient `Pic(C ×_k T) / π_T^* Pic(T)` inherits a canonical
136	abelian-group structure under which the quotient map is a surjective
137	homomorphism with kernel exactly `π_T^* Pic(T)`.
138	
139	Blueprint reference: `lem:rel_pic_sharp_groupoid` (Kleiman §2,
140	Defs. `df:aPf` + `df:Pfs`; Stacks tag 01CR). -/

144	The carrier setoid `RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup` is the **iso-class** equivalence
145	`Nonempty (L.carrier ≅ L'.carrier)` on the locally-trivial line bundles on `C ×_S T`,
146	*not* the quotient-by-`H_T` relation. Hence `Quotient (preimage_subgroup πC πT)` is

150	the *other* carrier, the `H_T`-quotient built in §1b below; they do not apply to the
151	iso-class carrier.

164	unit (`pullbackUnitIso`); compose to trivialise `(𝒪_X)|_W ≅ 𝒪_W`. -/

180	    Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Iso.refl N) e'.symm ≪≫

`PicSharp.addCommGroup` lives on `Quotient (RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup πC πT)`,
whose carrier setoid is the **iso-class** relation `Nonempty (L.carrier ≅ L'.carrier)` — i.e. the
**absolute** `Pic(C ×_S T)`. The blueprint (`lem:rel_pic_sharp_groupoid`, Kleiman §2 `df:Pfs`) asks
instead for the **relative** quotient `Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)`, the quotient by the subgroup
`H_T := im π_T^*`. This section builds that quotient directly as a coarser setoid
`relPicSetoid` on `LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT`, together with the abelian-group instance
`PicSharp.addCommGroup_via_tensorObj` on it.

**Relation (multiplicative form).** For `L L' : OnProduct πC πT` set
```
L ~ L'   ↔   ∃ N locally trivial on T,  L.carrier ≅ π_T^* N ⊗ L'.carrier,
```
where `π_T^* N = (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier`. This is the left-coset
relation of `H_T := im π_T^*`. It is **equivalent** to the blueprint's `L ⊗ L'^{-1} ≅ π_T^* N`
(tensor both sides by `L'` / its inverse), but the multiplicative form avoids naming the tensor
inverse of `L'` in the *definition* — only the setoid-symmetry step consumes a tensor inverse (of
`N` on the base `T`, via `Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse`). The blueprint statements
`lem:relpic_setoid_{refl,symm,trans}`, `lem:relpic_add_welldef` and `lem:pullback_inverse_iso`
are realized below in that multiplicative form. -/

/-- **The `H_T`-coset relation on `OnProduct πC πT`** (relative Picard, multiplicative form):
`L ~ L' ↔ ∃ N loc-triv on T, L.carrier ≅ π_T^* N ⊗ L'.carrier`. It encodes the
quotient `Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)` of `lem:rel_pic_sharp_groupoid`, and is coarser than the
absolute iso-class relation `RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup`. -/
def relPicRel {S C T : Scheme.{u}} (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S)
    (L L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) : Prop :=
  ∃ (N : T.Modules) (hN : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial N),
    Nonempty (L.carrier ≅
      Modules.tensorObj (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier L'.carrier)

/-- An isomorphism of the underlying bundles implies the `H_T`-coset relation (take `N = 𝒪_T`):
the relative relation is coarser than the absolute iso-class relation. Used to
transport the abelian-group axioms from the absolute iso-class group. -/
theorem relPicRel_of_iso {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
    {L L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT} (e : Nonempty (L.carrier ≅ L'.carrier)) :
    relPicRel πC πT L L' := by
  obtain ⟨e⟩ := e
  refine ⟨SheafOfModules.unit T.ringCatSheaf, isLocallyTrivial_unit, ⟨?_⟩⟩
  exact e ≪≫ (Modules.tensorObj_left_unitor L'.carrier).symm ≪≫
    Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Modules.pullbackUnitIso (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).symm
      (Iso.refl L'.carrier)

/-- **Reflexivity of the `H_T`-relation** (blueprint `lem:relpic_setoid_refl`): `L ~ L`, witnessed
by `N = 𝒪_T` and the pullback–unit iso `π_T^* 𝒪_T ≅ 𝒪_{C×T}` plus the left unitor. -/
theorem relPicRel_refl {S C T : Scheme.{u}} (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S)
    (L : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) : relPicRel πC πT L L :=
  relPicRel_of_iso ⟨Iso.refl _⟩

/-- **Symmetry of the `H_T`-relation** (blueprint `lem:relpic_setoid_symm`): from `L ~ L'` (via `N`)
get `L' ~ L` (via the tensor inverse `N⁻¹` on `T`), using multiplicativity of `π_T^*`, the
pullback–unit iso, and `Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse`. -/
theorem relPicRel_symm {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
    {L L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT} (h : relPicRel πC πT L L') :
    relPicRel πC πT L' L := by
  obtain ⟨N, hN, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨Ninv, hNinv, ⟨eN⟩⟩ := Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse hN
  refine ⟨Ninv, hNinv, ⟨?_⟩⟩
  -- `tensorObj (π_T^*Ninv) L ≅ L'`, then take `.symm`.
  refine Iso.symm ?_
  refine Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Iso.refl _) e ≪≫ ?_
  refine (Modules.tensorObj_assoc_iso
    (M := (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT Ninv hNinv).carrier)
    (N := (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier) (P := L'.carrier)).symm ≪≫ ?_
  refine Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso
    (Modules.pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT) Ninv N hNinv hN).symm
    (Iso.refl L'.carrier) ≪≫ ?_
  refine Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso
    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).mapIso
      (Modules.tensorObj_braiding Ninv N ≪≫ eN)) (Iso.refl L'.carrier) ≪≫ ?_
  exact Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Modules.pullbackUnitIso (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT))
    (Iso.refl L'.carrier) ≪≫ Modules.tensorObj_left_unitor L'.carrier

/-- **Transitivity of the `H_T`-relation** (blueprint `lem:relpic_setoid_trans`): from `L ~ L'` (via
`N`) and `L' ~ L''` (via `N'`) get `L ~ L''` via `N ⊗ N'`, using the associator and
multiplicativity of `π_T^*`. -/
theorem relPicRel_trans {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
    {L L' L'' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT}
    (h : relPicRel πC πT L L') (h' : relPicRel πC πT L' L'') :
    relPicRel πC πT L L'' := by
  obtain ⟨N, hN, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨N', hN', ⟨e'⟩⟩ := h'
  refine ⟨Modules.tensorObj N N', Modules.tensorObj_isLocallyTrivial hN hN', ⟨?_⟩⟩
  refine e ≪≫ Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Iso.refl _) e' ≪≫ ?_
  refine (Modules.tensorObj_assoc_iso
    (M := (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier)
    (N := (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N' hN').carrier) (P := L''.carrier)).symm ≪≫ ?_
  exact Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso
    (Modules.pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT) N N' hN hN').symm
    (Iso.refl L''.carrier)

/-- **The relative Picard carrier setoid** `Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)` (blueprint
`lem:rel_pic_sharp_groupoid`, carrier), the `H_T`-coset relation on `LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT`.
This is the RELATIVE quotient, distinct from the absolute iso-class
setoid `RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup`. -/
def relPicSetoid {S C T : Scheme.{u}} (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S) :
    Setoid (LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) where
  r := relPicRel πC πT
  iseqv := ⟨relPicRel_refl πC πT, relPicRel_symm, relPicRel_trans⟩

the associator and the braiding. Helper for `relPicRel_add`. -/

    ext a
    exact relFunctorial_id _C.hom T.unop.hom _ a
  map_comp {T T' T''} g h := by
    ext a

functor `PicSharp` to the relative functor `relPresheaf` (a group
homomorphism because the group laws on both sides descend the same tensor
operations; the `H_T`-relation is coarser than the iso-class relation by
`relPicRel_of_iso`). -/

    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 _C.hom] [IsProper _C.hom] :
    PicSharp _C ⟶ relPresheaf _C where

1	# Analogy: Pic⁰_{C/k} via ker(deg) instead of identity-component
2	
3	## Mode
4	api-alignment
5	
6	## Slug
7	pic0-ker-deg-pivot
8	
9	## Iteration
10	197
11	
12	## Question
13	
14	Should the project pivot from defining `Pic⁰_{C/k}` as `IdentityComponent
15	(PicScheme C)` (Stacks 04KU/04KV, parked ~4 iters at 0/it) to defining
16	it as `ker(deg : Pic_{C/k} → ℤ_{C/k})` (A.3.vii, gated)?
17	
18	## Project artifact(s)
19	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/IdentityComponent.lean:236-258` —
20	  `IdentityComponent` def (general substrate).
21	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/IdentityComponent.lean:737-743` —
22	  `Scheme.Pic0Scheme C` def (currently `sorry`; specialises substrate
23	  to `G = PicScheme C`).
24	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/IdentityComponent.lean:412-479` —
25	  `geometricallyConnected_of_connected_of_section`
26	  (Stacks 04KU helper; `sorry`-bodied, pending Stacks 037Q / 04KV
27	  substrate in Mathlib).
28	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/IdentityComponent.lean:779-784` —
29	  `PicScheme.degree` def (degree map on `k`-points, currently `sorry`).
30	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` — downstream
31	  consumer; uses `Pic0Scheme C : Over (Spec k)` opaquely.
32	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean:41-76` — further
33	  downstream consumer; uses `Pic0.jacobianScheme = (bundle C).scheme`
34	  with `Pic0Scheme` underlying.
35	
36	## Decisions identified
37	
38	The directive bundles two distinct decisions:
39	
40	1. **What is `Pic⁰_{C/k}` definitionally?** Identity-component (Stacks
41	   04KU/04KV) vs degree-zero open-and-closed subscheme (Kleiman
42	   `thm:Pphifin` + `ex:curves`)?
43	2. **Is there a Mathlib idiom for "kernel of a group-scheme
44	   morphism"** that the project should use directly?
45	
46	### Decision 1: Underlying scheme of `Pic⁰_{C/k}`
47	
48	- **Mathlib idiom**: NEITHER `IdentityComponent` of a group scheme NOR
49	  `ker(deg)` of a morphism of group schemes exists in Mathlib b80f227.
50	  Mathlib has `MonoidHom.ker` (sets / `Subgroup G`) but no
51	  scheme-level `GrpObj.ker`. Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel`
52	  requires `HasZeroMorphisms`, which `Scheme` does not satisfy
53	  (`Scheme` is cartesian-monoidal, not abelian). The **literature**
54	  has two equivalent definitions for smooth-proper-curve targets:
55	  Kleiman `prp:pic0` (identity component) and Kleiman
56	  `ex:curves` + Milne III.1 p.~87 (kernel of degree = `Pic⁰=Pic^0`).
57	- **Project's current path**: Identity-component via Stacks 04KU/04KV
58	  (parked, ~350 LOC pending Mathlib upstream `Stacks 037Q` /
59	  `04KV`).
60	- **Gap**: divergent-with-cost. The identity-component definition
61	  requires building project-side or upstream Mathlib infrastructure
62	  (`LocallyConnectedSpace` for locally-Noetherian schemes;
63	  `geometricallyConnected_of_connected_of_section`; descent of clopen
64	  partitions along fpqc base change). The degree-stratification
65	  definition only requires Kleiman §6 `thm:Pphifin` (the Hilbert-
66	  polynomial open-and-closed decomposition) and the curve-specific
67	  identification "leading coefficient of Hilbert polynomial = degree"
68	  (Riemann–Roch, RR.1).
69	- **Cost of divergence (current shipped path)**:
70	  - 2 typed sorries in `IdentityComponent.lean` (`geometricallyConnected_of_connected_of_section`,
71	    `IdentityComponent.baseChangeIso` iso slot) waiting on Stacks
72	    037Q / 04KV substrate not in Mathlib b80f227.
73	  - 1 typed sorry in `IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism`
74	    needing EGA IV₂ 4.5.8 (smooth × geom-conn → conn) + Stacks 04KU.
75	  - 1 typed sorry in `IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`
76	    needing the group-translation argument (EGA IV₂ 4.5.8/4.6.1).
77	  - Phase A.3.i parked at ~0/iter for 4 iters; ~350 LOC of
78	    Mathlib-upstream-grade work remaining.
79	- **Verdict**: **STRUCTURAL_OK** (pivot recommended).
80	
81	### Decision 2: Mathlib kernel idiom for `f : G → H` of group schemes
82	
83	- **Mathlib idiom**: No direct idiom. The category-theoretic shape
84	  ("kernel of a group-object morphism in a finite-limit category") is
85	  the pullback `pullback f (e_H ∘ !) : ker f ⟶ G`, where
86	  `e_H : 𝟙_C ⟶ H` is the identity of the target group object and
87	  `!` is the unique map to the terminal. Mathlib supports this
88	  IMPLICITLY via `CategoryTheory.Limits.HasPullbacks` on schemes, but
89	  does not package `GrpObj.ker` as a named construction.
90	  Closest precedents:
91	  - `MonoidHom.ker` (`Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Subgroup.Ker`): plain
92	    group homomorphism in Type, returns `Subgroup G`. Not applicable
93	    at scheme level.
94	  - `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker`
95	    (`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealSheaf.Basic`): kernel ideal
96	    sheaf of a scheme morphism, i.e. `Y.IdealSheafData` not a
97	    `Scheme`. A different concept (set-theoretic preimage of zero
98	    section, not the categorical fiber over the identity element).
99	  - `CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel`: requires `HasZeroMorphisms`, not
100	    applicable to `Scheme` or `Over (Spec k)`.
101	  - `MonoidHom.fiberEquivKer`: the categorical insight (kernel =
102	    fiber over identity), but in Type only.
103	- **Project's natural reframing**: The directive's "Pic⁰ := ker(deg)"
104	  framing is conceptual. The PRACTICAL construction is the
105	  degree-stratification:
106	  `PicScheme C = ∐_{d∈ℤ} Pic^d C` (Kleiman `ex:curves`), with
107	  `Pic⁰ := Pic^0` the degree-0 open-and-closed subscheme. This sidesteps
108	  the categorical-pullback definition entirely.
109	- **Gap**: NEEDS_MATHLIB_GAP_FILL (categorical `GrpObj.ker`) but with
110	  workaround: the degree-stratification gives the kernel directly,
111	  without invoking pullback-of-identity. The kernel is the union of
112	  connected components mapping to `0 ∈ ℤ`, and in the discrete
113	  codomain case this is just the preimage of an open-and-closed
114	  point.
115	- **Verdict**: **NEEDS_MATHLIB_GAP_FILL** for the abstract idiom, but
116	  not on the critical path: the project does not need to invoke a
117	  generic kernel construction, only the curve-specific
118	  decomposition. The "ker(deg)" framing in the directive should be
119	  read as a NAMING / MATHEMATICAL JUSTIFICATION for the degree-0
120	  component, not as a literal `kernel.lift` / `pullback.lift`
121	  invocation.
122	
123	## Confirmation of the equivalence "ker(deg) = identity component"
124	
125	### Kleiman §6, `ex:curves` (lines 4665–4681 of `references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex`)
126	
127	> *Assume $X/S$ is locally projective over $S$ and flat, and its
128	> geometric fibers are integral curves. Given an integer $m$, let
129	> $\Pic^m_{X/S} \subset \Pic_{X/S}$ be the set of points representing
130	> invertible sheaves $\mathcal L$ of degree $m$. Show the $\Pic^m_{X/S}$
131	> are open and closed subschemes of finite type; show they are
132	> disjoint and cover; and show that forming them commutes with
133	> changing $S$.*
134	>
135	> *Show there is no abuse of notation: the fiber of $\Pic^0_{X/S}$
136	> over $s\in S$ is the connected component of $0\in\Pic_{X_s/k_s}$.
137	> Show there is no torsion: $\Pic^0_{X/S}=\Pic^\tau_{X/S}$. Show each
138	> $\Pic^m_{X/S}$ is an fppf-torsor under $\Pic^0_{X/S}$.*
139	
140	This is the **direct citation** for `ker(deg) = identity component` on
141	smooth proper geometrically integral curves: the degree-0 component IS
142	the connected component of the identity. The project's curve hypotheses
143	(`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom + IsProper C.hom + GeometricallyIntegral C.hom`)
144	satisfy Kleiman's setup.
145	
146	### Milne III.1 (PDF p.~93 / book p.~87)
147	
148	> *Let $\Pic^r(C)$ be the set of divisor classes of degree $r$. For
149	> a fixed point $P_0$ on $C$, the map $[D]\mapsto[D+rP_0]:
150	> \Pic^0(C)\to\Pic^r(C)$ is a bijection **(both $\Pic^0(C)$ and
151	> $\Pic^r(C)$ are fibres of the map $\deg : \Pic(C)\to\Z$)**.*
152	
153	And p.~88:
154	> *We write $\Pic^0(C)$ for the group of isomorphism classes of
155	> invertible sheaves of degree zero on $C$.*
156	
157	This is the **textbook definition of `Pic⁰` for a curve**: kernel of
158	the degree map. Milne's Theorem 1.6 then says this functor `P_C^0` is
159	represented by an abelian variety (the Jacobian), with no detour
160	through identity-component theory at all.
161	
162	### Kleiman §6 `rmk:curves` (line 4682)
163	
164	> *There is another important case where $\Pic^0_{X/S}=\Pic^\tau_{X/S}$,
165	> namely, when $X$ is an Abelian $S$-scheme. [...]*
166	
167	Confirms the identification also holds in the abelian-scheme case
168	(used downstream when iterating to `Pic⁰` of `Pic⁰`).
169	
170	**Conclusion**: The equivalence `ker(deg) = identity component` is
171	mathematically standard, explicitly cited in both primary sources
172	(Kleiman) and the project's secondary reference (Milne). For the
173	project's curve hypothesis it is provable from Kleiman §6 alone,
174	WITHOUT invoking 04KU / 04KV.
175	
176	## Recommendation
177	
178	**Pivot to ker(deg)-style Pic⁰ via the degree-stratification**, with
179	concrete plan:
180	
181	1. **Repurpose `IdentityComponent.lean`** (or split into two files).
182	   The abstract `GroupScheme.IdentityComponent` substrate can stay
183	   for future use (no urgency to close its sorries — those are
184	   pure-Mathlib upstream-grade lemmas).
185	
186	2. **Add Kleiman `ex:curves` decomposition** as the substrate.
187	   Sketch (using Mathlib b80f227 instances `inferInstance` shape):
188	   ```lean
189	   /-- Kleiman ex:curves: the degree-`d` component of the Picard scheme
190	   of a smooth proper geom integral curve, as an open-and-closed
191	   subscheme of `PicScheme C`. -/
192	   noncomputable def PicScheme.degComp {k : Type u} [Field k]
193	       (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
194	       [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
195	       [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
196	       (d : ℤ) : Over (Spec (.of k)) := ...
197	
198	   /-- The open-and-closed inclusion `Pic^d_{C/k} ↪ Pic_{C/k}`. -/
199	   noncomputable def PicScheme.degComp.ι {k : Type u} [Field k]
200	       (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [...] (d : ℤ) :
201	       PicScheme.degComp C d ⟶ PicScheme C := ...
202	   ```
203	
204	3. **Redefine `Pic0Scheme C := PicScheme.degComp C 0`** in
205	   `IdentityComponent.lean` (or new file `Picard/Pic0ByDegree.lean`).
206	   The TYPE remains `Over (Spec k)`, so downstream consumers in
207	   `Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` and `Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean` are
208	   ABI-unchanged.
209	
210	4. **Inherit `GrpObj (Pic0Scheme C)`** from the multiplication on
211	   `PicScheme C`: `deg(L ⊗ M) = deg L + deg M`, so `Pic^0 × Pic^0 →
212	   Pic^0` via restricted multiplication. Closure under inverses:
213	   `deg(L⁻¹) = -deg L`, zero at degree 0. Identity: `O_C` has
214	   degree 0. Total LOC for the `GrpObj` instance: ~30–50.

217	   `Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible` in `Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`)
218	   STILL depends on identity-component theory in the long run
219	   (Kleiman `prp:pic0`), but with the pivot:
220	   - The statement no longer blocks the **definition** of `Pic⁰` or
221	     its downstream `Pic^0`-torsor structure.
222	   - The substrate "`Pic^0` connected over `k̄`" can be deferred or
223	     attacked via the same Stacks 04KU machinery in isolation.
224	   - Or, in characteristic zero, derived from `Pic^τ` finiteness +
225	     `Pic^0 = Pic^τ` (Kleiman `ex:curves`), bypassing 04KU entirely.
226	
227	6. **The "Pic⁰ = IdentityComponent" equivalence** becomes a separate
228	   theorem (currently captured loosely in
229	   `Pic0Scheme.kPoints_iff_kerDegree`), provable when 04KU/04KV land
230	   upstream. It is NOT on the critical path for
231	   `nonempty_jacobianWitness`.

9	# The degree on the relative Picard group over a field (gap G-D5(b), SB-5 descent gadgets)
10	
11	For the challenge curve `C : Over (Spec k)` and a field extension `K` of `k`, the relative
12	Picard group `relPic C (overSpec k K) = CechPic(C_K) ⧸ picFromBase` quotients out the classes
13	pulled back from `Spec K` — but `Spec K` is a one-point space, so its Čech Picard group is

16	Picard group:
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicDeg K : Additive (relPic C (overSpec k K)) →+ ℤ`, with the anchor
19	  `relPicDeg_relPicMk : relPicDeg K (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) L) = classDeg K L`;
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap` — **E-iv-alg descended to `relPic`**: the
21	  relative degree is invariant under restriction along `Spec` of any `k`-algebra map of
22	  field extensions, `relPicDeg K₂ (relPicAlgMap C φ x) = relPicDeg K₁ x`.
23

25	brick (SB-6) consumes `relPicDeg` and `relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap` verbatim — on a field
26	representative `(K', y)` of an étale-locally-trivial class, the honest degree is
27	`relPicDeg K' y`, well-defined across representatives by `relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap`.

42	
43	/-- **The degree vanishes on classes pulled back from the base field**: `Spec K` is a
44	one-point space, so its Čech Picard group is trivial and every class of `picFromBase` is
45	trivial. -/
46	theorem classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
47	    {L : (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic} (hL : L ∈ picFromBase C (overSpec k K)) :
48	    classDeg K L = 0 := by
49	  obtain ⟨N, rfl⟩ := (mem_picFromBase_iff C).mp hL
50	  haveI : Subsingleton (overSpec k K).left :=
51	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum K))
52	  rw [Scheme.CechPic.eq_one_of_subsingleton (overSpec k K).left N, map_one, classDeg_one]
53	
54	/-! ## The relative degree -/
55	
56	/-- **The degree on the relative Picard group over a field** (worksheet SB-5, first descent
57	gadget): `classDeg K` descends along `relPicMk` to the quotient
58	`relPic C (overSpec k K) = CechPic(C_K) ⧸ picFromBase`, because the Čech Picard group of the
59	one-point scheme `Spec K` is trivial.  The `degAt` brick (SB-6) reads the degree of a
60	field-representative of an étale-locally-trivial class through this homomorphism. -/
61	noncomputable def relPicDeg (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
62	    Additive (relPic C (overSpec k K)) →+ ℤ :=
63	  MonoidHom.toAdditiveLeft
64	    (QuotientGroup.lift (picFromBase C (overSpec k K))
65	      (AddMonoidHom.toMultiplicativeRight (classDeg K))
66	      (fun L hL => by
67	        have h0 : classDeg K L = 0 := classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase hL
68	        rw [MonoidHom.mem_ker]
69	        change Multiplicative.ofAdd (classDeg K L) = 1
70	        rw [h0, ofAdd_zero]))

72	/-- **The anchor of the relative degree**: on the class of `L`, the relative degree is
73	`classDeg K L`. -/

75	theorem relPicDeg_relPicMk (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
76	    (L : (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic) :
77	    relPicDeg K (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) L) = classDeg K L :=
78	  rfl

85	    [Algebra k K₂] (φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂) (x : relPic C (overSpec k K₁)) :
86	    relPicDeg K₂ (relPicAlgMap C φ x) = relPicDeg K₁ x := by
87	  induction x using relPic.ind with

91	          (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left) L) :=
92	      relPicMap_mk C (Over.overSpecMap φ) L
93	    rw [h1, relPicDeg_relPicMk, relPicDeg_relPicMk,
94	      classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition C φ L]

9	/-!
10	# The degree at field points and the degree-zero Picard functor (G-D6/G-D7, SB-7)
11	
12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).
30	  The restriction maps are `pic0Map`, with underlying-class equation `pic0Map_coe`
31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.
33	-/

48	/-! ## The degree at a field point -/
49	
50	/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
51	`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
52	algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
53	restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
54	def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
55	    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
56	  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
57	
58	section DegAt
59	
60	variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
61	
62	/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
63	@[simp]
64	theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
65	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
66	  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]
67	
68	/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
69	theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
70	    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
71	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
72	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
73	        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
74	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]
75	
76	/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
77	theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
78	    degAt lam⁻¹ t = -degAt lam t := by
79	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam⁻¹)) = -degAt lam t
80	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, PicEtAff.degAff_inv]
81	  rfl
82	
83	/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
84	restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
85	field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
86	degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
87	theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
88	    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
89	  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
90	      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
91	  rw [← picEtMap_comp]
92	
93	/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
94	theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
95	    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
96	    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
97	  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'
98	
99	end DegAt

101	/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/
102	
103	variable (C) in
104	/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
105	classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
106	degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
107	def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
108	  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
109	    degAt lam t = 0}
110	  one_mem' := by
111	    intro K _ _ t
112	    exact degAt_one t
113	  mul_mem' := by
114	    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
115	    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
116	  inv_mem' := by
117	    intro a ha K _ _ t
118	    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]
119	
120	/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
121	theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
122	    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
123	      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
124	          degAt lam t = 0 :=
125	  Iff.rfl
126	
127	variable (C) in
128	/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
129	of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
130	definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
131	points. -/
132	def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
133	    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
134	  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')
135	    fun lam K _ _ t' => (degAt_picEtMap f (lam : picEt C T) t').trans (lam.2 K (t' ≫ f))
136	
137	/-- The underlying étale Picard class of a restricted degree-zero class — the
138	naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/
139	@[simp]
140	theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
141	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :
142	    (pic0Map C f lam : picEt C T') = picEtMap C f (lam : picEt C T) :=
143	  rfl
144	
145	variable (C) in
146	/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
147	subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
148	of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of
149	the Wave-4 representability statement (design §2.7): the Jacobian represents *this*
150	functor. -/
151	def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
152	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
153	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)
154	  map_id T := by
155	    ext lam U
156	    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
157	  map_comp g h := by
158	    ext lam U
159	    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))
160	
161	@[simp]
162	theorem pic0Functor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
163	    (pic0Functor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :=
164	  rfl
165	
166	@[simp]
167	theorem pic0Functor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
168	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
169	    (pic0Functor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
170	  rfl
171	
172	variable (C) in
173	/-- The inclusion of the degree-zero subfunctor into the étale-sheafified relative
174	Picard functor, as a natural transformation — the naturality square consumers cite
175	(bundled form of `pic0Map_coe`). -/
176	def pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C where
177	  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Subgroup C T.unop).subtype
178	  naturality _ _ _ := rfl
179	
180	end

8	/-!
9	# Adelic Riemann–Roch — the multiplication isomorphism and class invariance
10	
11	This file supplies the **class-invariance layer** of the adelic χ-ledger: the
12	statement that all three numerical invariants of the ledger — `ℓ(D)`, `h¹(D)` and
13	`χ(D)` — depend only on the *linear-equivalence class* of `D`, together with the
14	elementary effective-witness dictionary that turns a nonzero global section into
15	an effective divisor in the same class.
16	
17	Everything here is **unconditional**: no gate class, no ledger exactness
18	hypothesis, no finiteness input.  The only mechanism is that multiplication by a
19	nonzero rational function `g ∈ K(X)^×` is a `k`-linear automorphism of `K(X)`
20	which carries the section subspace `Γ(U, 𝒪(D))` *onto* `Γ(U, 𝒪(D − div g))`.
21	
22	## Main declarations
23	
24	* `Adelic.mul_mem_sectionOfDivisor` — the order computation
25	  `ord_P (g·f) = ord_P g + ord_P f`, in section-membership form: the single
26	  arithmetic fact behind everything else in this file.
27	* `Adelic.mulEquivFunctionField` — multiplication by `g ≠ 0` as a `k`-linear
28	  automorphism of `K(X)` (`k` a field of constants).
29	* `Adelic.map_sectionSub_mulEquiv` — `(Γ(U, 𝒪(D))).map (g·) = Γ(U, 𝒪(D'))`
30	  whenever `D'(P) = D(P) − ord_P g` for every prime divisor `P`.
31	* `Adelic.sectionSubMulEquiv` — the resulting `k`-linear isomorphism
32	  `Γ(U, 𝒪(D)) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(U, 𝒪(D'))`.
33	* `Adelic.ell_eq_of_shift`, `Adelic.h1dim_eq_of_shift`, `Adelic.chi_eq_of_shift`
34	  — `ℓ`, `h¹` and `χ` are invariant under the shift `D ↦ D − div g`.
35	* `Adelic.chi_eq_of_principal_shift`, `Adelic.chi_eq_of_linearEquivalence`
36	  — the same statements spelled with `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal` and with the
37	  project's `LinearEquivalence` relation.
38	* `Adelic.exists_effective_linearEquiv_of_ne_zero_mem` — the effective-witness
39	  brick: a nonzero `f ∈ L(D)` exhibits `D + div f ≥ 0` in the class of `D`.
40	* `Adelic.one_le_ell_of_nonneg` — conversely an effective divisor has `ℓ ≥ 1`.
41	
42	## Provenance
43	
44	The mathematical content is the adelic (function-field) incarnation of the
45	sibling project's sheaf-theoretic `mulEquivDivisorSheaf` /
46	`chi_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq` pair
47	(`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`, `RiemannRoch/MulEquiv.lean` and
48	`RiemannRoch/Degree.lean`).  **No code was ported**: that development is built on
49	a different substrate (`CurveDivisor` on closed points, `divisorSheaf`,
50	`Sheaf.chi`, `CechPic`), none of whose names exist in this project.  What is
51	reused is the *argument*: transport `χ` along multiplication by `g` and cancel in
52	the ledger.  Here the transport is elementary linear algebra on subspaces of
53	`K(X)`, which is why this file needs no finiteness or exactness input at all —
54	whereas the sheaf-theoretic form needs the χ-additivity machinery even to state
55	the transport.
56	-/

72	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
73	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]

75	/-- **Multiplication by `g` shifts the section bound by `div g`.**  If
76	`D'(P) ≥ D(P) − ord_P g` at every prime divisor `P` of `U`, then multiplication
77	by `g ≠ 0` carries `Γ(U, 𝒪(D))` into `Γ(U, 𝒪(D'))`.
78	
79	This is `ord_P (g·f) = ord_P g + ord_P f` (`order_mul_of_ne_zero`) rearranged:
80	`ord_P (g·f) ≥ ord_P g − D(P) ≥ −D'(P)`.  Stated with an inequality rather than
81	an equality on `D'` so that the same lemma serves both directions of the
82	isomorphism (apply it to `g⁻¹` for the inverse). -/
83	theorem mul_mem_sectionOfDivisor {U : X.Opens} {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
84	    {g : X.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0)
85	    (hD' : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, P.point ∈ U →
86	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P - Scheme.RationalMap.order P g ≤

curve `C` has residue field `k̄`, so each prime divisor `[P]` contributes degree
one to the sum, and `deg(D) := Σᵢ nᵢ` is the sum of the integer coefficients of
the formal sum `D = Σ nᵢ · [Pᵢ]`.

(Over a general field `k` one weights by the residue-field degrees
`Σᵢ nᵢ · [κ(Pᵢ) : k]` to recover the geometric degree; the project's RR bridge
needs only the `k̄` specialisation.)

Blueprint reference: `def:divisor_degree` (Hartshorne II §6 p. 137; Stacks 0BE0).

Implementation: `Finsupp.sum D (fun _ n => n)` is the sum of all coefficients of
the finitely supported function representing `D`. -/

`deg(D₁ + D₂) = deg(D₁) + deg(D₂)`, `deg(-D) = -deg(D)`, `deg(0) = 0`. Bundled
as an `AddMonoidHom` for downstream use (the linear-equivalence quotient

* `IsRegularLocalRing` : A Noetherian local ring is regular if
  `(maximalIdeal R).spanFinrank = ringKrullDim R`,

* `IsRegularRing` : A noetherian ring is regular if its localization at any prime
  `IsRegularLocalRing`.

public section

open IsLocalRing

/-- A Noetherian local ring is said to be regular if its maximal ideal
can be generated by `dim R` elements. -/
@[stacks 00KU]
class IsRegularLocalRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : Prop extends
    IsLocalRing R, IsNoetherianRing R where
  spanFinrank_maximalIdeal : (maximalIdeal R).spanFinrank = ringKrullDim R

variable (R : Type*) [CommRing R]

lemma isRegularLocalRing_iff [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    IsRegularLocalRing R ↔ (maximalIdeal R).spanFinrank = ringKrullDim R :=
  ⟨fun ⟨h⟩ ↦ h, fun h ↦ ⟨h⟩⟩

namespace IsRegularLocalRing

lemma of_spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_le [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (le : (maximalIdeal R).spanFinrank ≤ ringKrullDim R) : IsRegularLocalRing R :=
  (isRegularLocalRing_iff _).mpr (le_antisymm le (ringKrullDim_le_spanFinrank_maximalIdeal R))

variable {R} in
lemma of_ringEquiv [IsRegularLocalRing R] {R' : Type*} [CommRing R']
    (e : R ≃+* R') : IsRegularLocalRing R' := by
  have := e.isLocalRing
  have := isNoetherianRing_of_ringEquiv R e
  rwa [isRegularLocalRing_iff, ← ringKrullDim_eq_of_ringEquiv e, ← map_ringEquiv_maximalIdeal e,
    Ideal.spanFinrank_map_eq_of_ringEquiv, ← isRegularLocalRing_iff]

lemma iff_finrank_cotangentSpace [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    IsRegularLocalRing R ↔ Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R) = ringKrullDim R := by
  rw [isRegularLocalRing_iff, spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace]

instance [IsLocalRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsPrincipalIdealRing R] : IsRegularLocalRing R := by
  by_cases isf : IsField R
  · let := isf.toField
    simp [isRegularLocalRing_iff, maximalIdeal_eq_bot]
  · apply of_spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_le
    rcases IsPrincipalIdealRing.principal (maximalIdeal R) with ⟨x, hx⟩
    simpa only [(IsPrincipalIdealRing.ringKrullDim_eq_one R) isf,
      Nat.cast_le_one, ← Set.ncard_singleton x, hx] using
        Submodule.spanFinrank_span_le_ncard_of_finite (Set.finite_singleton x)

end IsRegularLocalRing

/-- A noetherian ring is regular if its localization at any prime `IsRegularLocalRing`. -/
class IsRegularRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : Prop extends IsNoetherianRing R where
  isRegularLocalRing_localization (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p)
